title: The release rollback ships its revert with no commit-gate attestation, so the revert probably stays local
routed_reason: the release pipeline is console-built, and a fix needs a design decision about the rollback provenance
source: console, 2026-10-08, the review of the v22.27.0 docs alignment (observation O2; the reviewer read the code and did not run it)
summary: When the marketplace poll fails after the push, the release pipeline rolls back. go/internal/releasepipeline/rollback.go:339-341 ships the revert with evolve ship --class manual and EVOLVE_SHIP_AUTO_CONFIRM, but it gives no commit-gate attestation and no --bypass-commit-gate. ship/commitgate.go:58-66 (verifyCommitGateAttestation) refuses a manual ship with no attestation. Thus the revert probably stays local, and the rollback reports PARTIAL (local-only), while the bad release stays on origin.
fix: Write a red-first test that drives the real rollback through ship with a fake remote and asserts that the revert reaches origin. Then give the rollback revert its own provenance: a release-class or rollback-class ship that the commit gate accepts with a recorded reason, or a gate attestation that the pipeline writes for its own revert. Do not use --bypass-commit-gate for routine use.
acceptance: A test proves that the rollback revert reaches origin through the real ship path (red first)
The rollback provenance is recorded in the ledger, and the commit gate stays on for every other manual ship
docs/guides/publishing-releases.md describes the rollback as it runs
